page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with one small italic marginal note in the left margin beside the line "citur proprie". Running head at the top, page number 222 at the top left of the text block, catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: industria hominum. Et quidem vel e Radice, vel Stolone sive surculo.
Radice, scilicet in terra depressa: hæ facile alimentum e terra attrahere & vivere possunt.
Stolone sive surculo vel terræ infixo, vel plantæ trunco.
Terra infixo: ut Rosa, Salix, Vitis, &c.
Planta trunco, videlicet intrusione surculi, inter lignum & corticem, & di-Infitio,citur proprie Infitio, Græcè ἐμφύτευσις[?].
Quamvis quædam plantæ omnibus his modis propagentur.
Atq; hi sunt propagationis modi artificiales frequentiores: præter quos illé quoq; est longè rarior, quo folium terræ infossum germinat in novam prolem.

p.i: Ea pars Rami, quæ terræ infoditur, in se conservat caloris, humoris atq; adeò animæ vim, & attractio humore intumescit, & spiritum concipit: detenta verò vis animæ & caloris ope adjuta, partes humoris grauissimas deorsum distribuit, unde radices efformantur, & leuissimas sursum, unde alitur superficies.
Eadem fere est ratio in insitione: sicut enim stirpes ex terra tanquam utero; ita infi[?]-

page.notes: Left margin note "Infitio," printed in italic, placed beside the line "citur proprie". Greek word "ἐμφύτευσις" is partly uncertain, marked [?]. The word after "in" at the line end of "in se conservat" is taken as "se". The final word "infi-" at the page foot is uncertain, marked [?]. The catchword at the lower right ("ta") is uncertain. Faint show-through text in both margins and at the foot is ignored.
